label: Opinion of a culture
summary: Changes how much characters with this modifier like people of one culture.
details: `$CULTURE$` stands for the key of a culture, for example `<culture key>_opinion`. Vanilla defines these as plain numbers (not percentages), so the amount is a flat opinion change that can be negative. The direction (who likes whom) comes from the name; the game documents nothing more. Works on characters.

label: Opinion of a faith
summary: Changes how much characters with this modifier like people who follow one faith.
details: `$FAITH$` stands for a faith or religion key as the game's modifier list names it, for example `<faith key>_opinion`. A flat opinion change that can be negative, as in vanilla's religion opinion modifiers. The direction (who likes whom) comes from the name. Works on characters.

label: Development growth in a region
summary: Adds to how fast development grows in the lands of one geographical region.
details: `$GEOGRAPHICAL_REGION$` stands for the key of a region, for example `<region key>_development_growth`. Vanilla shows it as a flat number, while the `_factor` form is a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Development growth factor in a region
summary: Scales, by a percentage, how fast development grows in the lands of one geographical region.
details: `$GEOGRAPHICAL_REGION$` stands for the key of a region, for example `<region key>_development_growth_factor`. Vanilla shows it as a percentage, unlike the flat plain `_development_growth` form. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Vassal herd contribution, base
summary: Adds to the base herd that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. The game's own name for it is "vassal herd base contribution"; herd is the nomadic resource. The unit is not documented. Works on characters.

label: Vassal herd contribution
summary: Scales the herd that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. The game's own name for it is "vassal herd contribution", the multiplier counterpart of the base one. The unit is not documented. Works on characters.

label: Vassal levy contribution, base
summary: Adds to the base levy (soldiers) that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type; vanilla's keys use a form like `feudal_government`. Vanilla shows both the base and the multiplier forms as percentages. Works on characters.

label: Vassal levy contribution
summary: Scales the levy (soldiers) that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type; vanilla's keys use a form like `feudal_government`. The base form is `_levy_contribution_add`. Works on characters.

label: Opinion of a government type
summary: Changes how much characters with this modifier like rulers of one government type.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type; vanilla's keys use a form like `feudal_government_opinion`. A flat opinion change that can be negative (vanilla defines it as a plain number). The direction comes from the name; the game documents nothing more. Works on characters.

label: Same-faith government opinion
summary: Changes how much characters with this modifier like rulers of one government type who share their faith.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. The game names the clan version "ruler of same faith opinion". A flat opinion change that can be negative. Works on characters.

label: Vassal prestige contribution, base
summary: Adds to the base prestige that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. The game's own name for the generic form is "vassal prestige base contribution". The unit is not documented. Works on characters.

label: Vassal prestige contribution
summary: Scales the prestige that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. The game's own name for the generic form is "vassal prestige contribution". The unit is not documented. Works on characters.

label: Vassal tax contribution, base
summary: Adds to the base tax that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. Vanilla shows both the base and the multiplier forms as percentages. Works on characters.

label: Vassal tax contribution
summary: Scales the tax that vassals of one government type contribute.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. The base form is `_tax_contribution_add`. Works on characters.

label: Tributary opinion by government
summary: Changes opinion between a ruler and tributaries, for one government type.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. Going by its name it concerns tributaries (rulers who pay tribute); which side's opinion changes, and of whom, is not documented. A flat opinion change. Works on characters.

label: Vassal opinion by government
summary: Changes opinion between a ruler and vassals, for one government type.
details: `$GOVERNMENT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a government type. Going by its name it concerns vassals; which side's opinion changes, and of whom, is not documented. A flat opinion change. Works on characters.

label: Holding building gold cost
summary: Changes the gold cost of constructing buildings in holdings of one holding type.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. The game names this "Castle buildings construction cost". It is a percentage. Compare `_holding_build_gold_cost`, which is for the holding itself. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding building piety cost
summary: Changes the piety cost of constructing buildings in holdings of one holding type.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. It is a percentage. Compare `_holding_build_piety_cost`, which is for the holding itself. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding building prestige cost
summary: Changes the prestige cost of constructing buildings in holdings of one holding type.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. It is a percentage. Compare `_holding_build_prestige_cost`, which is for the holding itself. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding building time
summary: Changes how long constructing buildings in holdings of one holding type takes.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. The game names this "Castle buildings construction time". It is a percentage. Compare `_holding_build_speed`, which is for the holding itself. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding gold cost by type
summary: Changes the gold cost of constructing a holding of one holding type.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. The game names this "Castle holding construction cost". It is a percentage. Unlike `_build_gold_cost`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding piety cost by type
summary: Changes the piety cost of constructing a holding of one holding type.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. It is a percentage. Unlike `_build_piety_cost`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding prestige cost by type
summary: Changes the prestige cost of constructing a holding of one holding type.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. It is a percentage. Unlike `_build_prestige_cost`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Holding build time by type
summary: Changes how long constructing a holding of one holding type takes.
details: `$HOLDING_TYPE$` stands for the key of a holding type, written like `castle_holding`. The game names this "Castle holding construction time". It is a percentage. Unlike `_build_speed`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Lifestyle experience gain, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the experience a character gains in one lifestyle.
details: `$LIFESTYLE$` stands for a lifestyle key as vanilla writes it, for example `martial_lifestyle_xp_gain_add`. The game names it "Martial lifestyle experience gain". A plain number. Works on characters.

label: Lifestyle experience gain, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the experience a character gains in one lifestyle.
details: `$LIFESTYLE$` stands for a lifestyle key as vanilla writes it, for example `martial_lifestyle_xp_gain_mult`. Shown as a percentage; negative values slow experience down. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms damage, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the damage of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type, for example `heavy_infantry_damage_add`. Works on characters, so it applies to the units of whoever has it.

label: Men-at-arms damage, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the damage of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type, for example `heavy_infantry_damage_mult`. Works on characters, so it applies to the units of whoever has it.

label: Men-at-arms upkeep, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the upkeep (gold) of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Vanilla shows it as a gold percentage where an increase is bad, so a negative value makes the units cheaper to keep. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms size, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the maximum size of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type, for example `heavy_infantry_max_size_add`. A plain number. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms size, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the maximum size of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Shown as a percentage. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms pursuit, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the pursuit stat of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type, for example `light_cavalry_pursuit_add`. Pursuit is one of the unit's combat stats; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms pursuit, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the pursuit stat of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Pursuit is one of the unit's combat stats; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms hiring cost, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the gold cost of recruiting one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Vanilla shows it as a gold percentage where an increase is bad, so a negative value makes hiring cheaper. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms screen, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the screen stat of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Screen is one of the unit's combat stats; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms screen, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the screen stat of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Screen is one of the unit's combat stats; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms siege progress, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the siege progress contributed by one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. The game labels it "siege progress" (for example for heavy infantry). Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms siege progress, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the siege progress contributed by one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. The game labels it "siege progress". Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms toughness, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the toughness stat of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Toughness is one of the unit's combat stats; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Men-at-arms toughness, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the toughness stat of one men-at-arms unit type.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a unit type. Toughness is one of the unit's combat stats; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Opinion of a religion
summary: Changes how much characters with this modifier like followers of one religion.
details: `$RELIGIOUS$` stands for the key of a religion, written like vanilla's `islam_religion_opinion`. A flat opinion change that can be negative. The direction comes from the name; the game documents nothing more. Works on characters.

label: Opinion of a religious family
summary: Changes how much characters with this modifier like followers of one religious family.
details: `$RELIGIOUS_FAMILY$` stands for the key of a religion family (a group of related religions), written like vanilla's `rf_pagan_opinion`. A flat opinion change that can be negative. The direction comes from the name. Works on characters.

label: Enemy scheme phase length
summary: Adds days to each phase of schemes of one type that other people run against the character.
details: `$SCHEME_TYPE$` stands for the key of a scheme type, for example `claim_throne_enemy_scheme_phase_duration_add`. The game labels it "Enemy [scheme] speed" and shows positive values as days slower per scheme phase. Which schemes count as "enemy" comes from the name. Works on characters.

label: Scheme phase length
summary: Adds days to each phase of the character's schemes of one type.
details: `$SCHEME_TYPE$` stands for the key of a scheme type, for example `befriend_scheme_phase_duration_add`. Vanilla shows positive values as days slower per scheme phase, so a negative value speeds the scheme up. Works on characters.

label: Situation supply limit, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the supply limit within one situation.
details: `$SITUATION_TYPE$` stands for the key of a situation; vanilla has for example `the_great_steppe_supply_limit_add`, labelled "supply limit in the Great Steppe". Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Situation supply limit, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the supply limit within one situation.
details: `$SITUATION_TYPE$` stands for the key of a situation. Going by the `_mult` name it is the percentage version of `_supply_limit_add`. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Tax slot count
summary: Adds to the number of tax slots of one tax slot type.
details: `$TAX_SLOT_TYPE$` stands for the key of a tax slot type. Vanilla's `clan_tax_slot_add` is labelled "available tax jurisdictions". Works on characters.

label: Terrain advantage
summary: Adds advantage when fighting on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain, for example `plains_advantage`. The game labels it "advantage in Plains" (a command modifier, so it applies to armies the character leads). A plain number. Works on characters.

label: Terrain attrition, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the attrition suffered on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Vanilla shows it as a percentage where an increase is bad, so a negative value reduces attrition. Works on characters.

label: Terrain barter goods, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the barter goods tied to one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game labels it "<terrain> barter goods" and documents nothing more. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Cancel terrain supply penalty
summary: Cancels the supply limit penalty of one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain, for example `desert_cancel_negative_supply`. The game labels it "negate supply limit penalty in Desert" (a command modifier). Works on characters.

label: Terrain building gold cost
summary: Changes by a percentage the gold cost of constructing buildings on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game labels it "building construction cost in Plains". Vanilla shows it as a percentage where an increase is bad. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain building piety cost
summary: Changes by a percentage the piety cost of constructing buildings on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Shares the "building construction cost" text with the gold form. Vanilla shows it as a percentage where an increase is bad. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain building prestige cost
summary: Changes by a percentage the prestige cost of constructing buildings on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Shares the "building construction cost" text with the gold form. Vanilla shows it as a percentage where an increase is bad. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain development growth, flat
summary: Adds to how fast development grows on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Vanilla shows it as a flat number; the `_factor` form is a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain development growth, percent
summary: Scales, by a percentage, how fast development grows on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Vanilla shows it as a percentage, unlike the flat `_development_growth` form. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain fertility consumption, flat
summary: Adds to how fast county fertility is used up on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game's generic text for this modifier is "county fertility consumption". The terrain link and the unit come from the key; the game documents nothing more. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain fertility consumption, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage how fast county fertility is used up on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game's generic text for this modifier is "county fertility consumption". The game documents nothing more. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain fertility growth, flat
summary: Adds to how fast county fertility grows on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game's generic text for this modifier is "county fertility growth". The game documents nothing more. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain fertility growth, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage how fast county fertility grows on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game's generic text for this modifier is "county fertility growth". The game documents nothing more. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain holding gold cost
summary: Changes by a percentage the gold cost of constructing a holding on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game labels it "holding construction cost in Plains". Unlike `_construction_gold_cost`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Vanilla shows it as a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain holding piety cost
summary: Changes by a percentage the piety cost of constructing a holding on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Shares the "holding construction cost" text with the gold form. Unlike `_construction_piety_cost`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain holding prestige cost
summary: Changes by a percentage the prestige cost of constructing a holding on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Shares the "holding construction cost" text with the gold form. Unlike `_construction_prestige_cost`, it is about the holding itself, not its buildings. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain levy size, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the levy size on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game labels it "levy size in Plains"; vanilla shows it as a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain maximum combat roll
summary: Changes the highest combat roll possible when fighting on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain, for example `desert_max_combat_roll`. The game labels it "maximum combat roll in Desert" (a command modifier). A plain number. Works on characters.

label: Terrain minimum combat roll
summary: Changes the lowest combat roll possible when fighting on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Going by its name it is the counterpart of `_max_combat_roll`; vanilla defines it as a plain number. Works on characters.

label: Terrain provisions use, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage how many provisions are used on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game labels it "<terrain> provisions use". Vanilla shows it as a percentage where an increase is bad, so a negative value saves provisions. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain supply limit, flat
summary: Adds a flat amount to the supply limit on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Vanilla shows it as a plain number; the `_mult` form is a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain supply limit, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the supply limit on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. Vanilla shows it as a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain holding tax, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the tax of holdings on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain. The game labels it "holding taxes in Plains"; vanilla shows it as a percentage. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Terrain travel danger
summary: Changes the travel danger on one terrain type.
details: `$TERRAIN_TYPE$` stands for the key of a terrain, for example `hills_travel_danger`. Vanilla shows it as a plain number where an increase is bad. Works on characters, provinces and counties.

label: Trait track XP degradation, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the monthly experience degradation of one trait track.
details: `$TRAIT_TRACK$` stands for the key of a trait with an experience track, for example `pilgrim_xp_degradation_mult`. The game labels it "monthly <trait> trait level track XP degradation". Works on characters.

label: Trait track XP gain, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage how fast experience in one trait track is gained.
details: `$TRAIT_TRACK$` stands for the key of a trait with an experience track. The game documents nothing beyond the name and the `_mult` (percentage) form; positive values speed gain up. Works on characters.

label: Trait track XP loss, percent
summary: Changes by a percentage the experience lost in one trait track.
details: `$TRAIT_TRACK$` stands for the key of a trait with an experience track. Which losses count is not documented, and vanilla has no text for it. Works on characters.

details: `$VASSAL_STANCE$` stands for the key of a vassal stance, for example `glory_hound_ai_boldness`. The game labels it as the stance's personality boldness; vanilla defines it as a plain number. Works on characters.

summary: Changes the AI compassion personality value tied to one vassal stance.
details: `$VASSAL_STANCE$` stands for the key of a vassal stance. Same pattern as `_ai_boldness`; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Stance AI energy
summary: Changes the AI energy personality value tied to one vassal stance.
details: `$VASSAL_STANCE$` stands for the key of a vassal stance. Same pattern as `_ai_boldness`; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Stance AI greed
summary: Changes the AI greed personality value tied to one vassal stance.
details: `$VASSAL_STANCE$` stands for the key of a vassal stance. Same pattern as `_ai_boldness`; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Stance AI honor
summary: Changes the AI honor personality value tied to one vassal stance.
details: `$VASSAL_STANCE$` stands for the key of a vassal stance. Same pattern as `_ai_boldness`; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.

label: Stance AI rationality
summary: Changes the AI rationality personality value tied to one vassal stance.
details: `$VASSAL_STANCE$` stands for the key of a vassal stance. Same pattern as `_ai_boldness`; the game documents nothing more here. Works on characters.
